title: The rule: out and back take equal times
spoken: The outward assigned travel time equals the return assigned travel time.
explanation: This is a definition of what B's clock should read, not a law found by measurement: it sets the time light takes from A to B equal to the time it takes from B back to A.
assumptions: Clocks A and B are at rest in the same system, and a light signal goes from A to B, is reflected, and returns to A.
Equal travel times out and back is the definition of B's reading, not a measurement: nothing timed at one place can test it.
Modern teaching notation. The paper writes the return reading as t′_A; here it is t_A,return, so that a prime keeps meaning the moving system.

notes.title: Time assigned to the return trip
notes.explanation: A's return reading minus B's reading: how long the light is said to take from B back to A.

notes.title: Time assigned to the outward trip
notes.explanation: B's reading minus A's departure reading: how long the light is said to take from A to B.

notes.title: Set the two equal
notes.explanation: Requiring the two trips to take equal times is the synchronization convention. It could be chosen otherwise without contradicting any single measurement at A or B.

notes.title: Reading at A as the signal leaves
notes.explanation: Clock A's reading at the moment the light signal leaves A. It is read at A, where the event happens, so no convention is needed to know it.

notes.title: The reading B is to show
notes.explanation: Clock B's reading at the reflection. This is the unknown the rule is for: B is far from A, so A's clock cannot be read at that event.

notes.title: The reading B is to show
notes.explanation: Clock B's reading at the reflection. This is the unknown the rule is for: B is far from A, so A's clock cannot be read at that event.

notes.title: Reading at A when the signal is back
notes.explanation: Clock A's reading when the reflected signal arrives back at A. Also read locally, at the event.
